q: What is the generic name of Item A?
n: Item A is a roof drain: a drain body with a domed strainer set in the roof deck, so leaves and debris do not enter the leader pipe. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drainage); ASME A112.6.4 (roof drains).

q: What is Item B, which is installed on a parapet wall?
n: A scupper is an opening or drain through a parapet wall that lets roof water spill out to a leader or overflow. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drainage); SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual.

q: Made of stainless steel, Item C is typically used in which area of the house?
n: Stainless steel linear or square floor drains with fine grates are typical of shower areas, where they resist corrosion and look neat. Source: Plumbing fixture manufacturer literature; ASME A112.6.3 (floor drains).

q: What is Item D?
n: Item D is the drain grate, the removable perforated cover over the drain body that admits water and keeps out solids. Source: ASME A112.6.3 (floor and trench drains).

q: What is Item E, which is used for maintenance purposes?
n: A cleanout is a plugged access fitting in a drain line, so rods or snakes can be inserted to clear blockages during maintenance. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (cleanouts).

q: Identify what type of vent is shown in Image A.
n: A circuit vent serves a battery of two to eight fixtures, connected from the last fixture on a horizontal branch to the vent stack. Image A shows this. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents); Uniform Plumbing Code.

q: Identify what type of vent is shown in Image B.
n: A branch vent connects one or more individual vents to the vent stack or stack vent. Image B shows this. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: Identify what type of vent is shown in Image C.
n: An individual (back) vent serves one fixture trap and connects to the vent system above the fixture. Image C shows this. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: Identify what type of vent is shown in Image D.
n: A vent stack is a vertical vent pipe running through floors that provides air circulation to and from the drainage system. Image D shows it. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: Identify what type of vent is shown in Image E.
n: A common vent serves two fixture traps connected at the same level, such as back-to-back lavatories. Image E shows this. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: Rubber couplings with gear clamps join which pipe?
n: Hubless (no-hub) cast iron soil pipe is joined with neoprene sleeves clamped by stainless steel gear-band couplings. Source: CISPI 310 (hubless cast iron couplings); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Electrofusion joins which pipe?
n: HDPE pipe is joined by fusion. Electrofusion fittings have embedded heating coils that melt and fuse the pipe and fitting together. Source: ASTM F1055 (electrofusion fittings for PE pipe).

q: Solvent cement is used to connect which type of pipe?
n: PVC pipe is joined with solvent cement, which softens and chemically welds the pipe and socket together. Source: ASTM D2564 (solvent cements for PVC); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: A rubber gasket is used to connect which type of pipe?
n: Hubless cast iron pipe joints use a rubber (neoprene) gasket sleeve under a stainless steel clamp. Compression gaskets are also used for hub cast iron. Source: CISPI 310; ASTM C564 (rubber gaskets for cast iron soil pipe).

q: Lead and oakum join which pipe?
n: Hub-and-spigot cast iron joints are caulked: oakum is packed into the hub and molten lead poured and caulked over it. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (joints); CISPI Cast Iron Soil Pipe Handbook.

q: What is a passage under a road, embankment or canal that lets water through?
n: A culvert is a pipe or box passage under a road, embankment or canal that lets a stream or drainage water pass through. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines (culverts); FHWA Hydraulic Design of Culverts.

q: What device in a drain line keeps storm water or sewage from flowing back into the building's drainage?
n: A backwater valve is a check-type valve in the building drain that closes when the public sewer surcharges, preventing sewage from flowing back into low fixtures. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (backwater valves).

q: Besides sanitary sewers, public sewers are also classed as:
n: Public sewers are either sanitary sewers (wastewater) or storm sewers (rainwater), and combined sewers carry both. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions); Metcalf & Eddy, Wastewater Engineering.

q: Storm drains are categorized into three: the inside storm drain, the outside storm drain, and the ___:
n: Storm drains are classified as inside, outside and overhead (roof) storm drains, the last collecting water from roofs and decks. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drainage).

q: Which is NOT a rule of thumb for drainage design?
o: Run pipes as straight as possible
Lay buried drains on compacted soil
n: Drains are not run under driveways if it can be avoided, since vehicle loads can crush them and access for repairs is hard. The other choices are standard rules. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is the semi-solid sediment that settles at the bottom of a septic tank?
n: Sludge is the semi-solid matter that settles at the bottom of a septic tank. Scum floats on top and effluent is the clarified liquid. Source: US EPA Onsite Wastewater Treatment Systems Manual; NPCP (septic tanks).

q: If a septic tank has a compartment exceeding 3.7 meters in length, what additional requirement is needed?
o: Increase in the number of compartments
A baffle wall must be added
Increase in the number of leaching chambers
n: Where a septic tank compartment is longer than about 3.7 m (12 ft), an additional manhole is required so every part of the tank can be reached for inspection and desludging. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tank access).

q: What is an alternative to the conventional septic tank?
n: An aerobic treatment unit injects air so bacteria digest the waste faster and more completely than in a septic tank. It is an approved alternative to conventional septic systems. Source: US EPA Onsite Wastewater Treatment Systems Manual; NSF/ANSI 40.

q: Which of the following has a similar function but serves a different purpose?
n: A grease trap and a septic tank both separate floating and settling matter from wastewater by detention, but the trap retains kitchen grease while the septic tank treats sewage. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (interceptors and septic tanks).

q: What type of material is typically used for the base of a septic tank?
n: A septic tank's base is a reinforced concrete slab, so it carries the tank's weight and earth pressure and stays watertight. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tank construction); DOH sanitation guidelines.

q: A vent that allows air circulation between the drainage and venting systems by connecting a vent stack to a horizontal drain between the first fixture and the soil or waste stack is called a:
n: A relief vent connects the vent stack to the horizontal drain between the first fixture and the stack, letting air circulate and relieving pressure in the branch. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: An individual vent for a fixture, taken off downstream of its trap, is a:
n: A back vent is an individual vent taken off the trap arm downstream of the fixture trap, rising to connect with the vent system. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vents).

q: What is the general term for any pipe that ventilates a plumbing system?
n: Vent pipe is the general term for any pipe that ventilates the drainage system and protects trap seals. Vent stacks and branch vents are kinds of vent pipe. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).

q: How far above the fixture's flood rim must a vent rise before running horizontally?
n: A vent must rise at least 150 mm (6 in.) above the fixture's flood-level rim before running horizontally, so it is never flooded with waste. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (vent installation); Uniform Plumbing Code Sec. 905.

q: What keeps sewer odors from coming out of fixture drains?
n: A trap such as a P-trap holds a water seal in its bend that blocks sewer gases from entering the room through the fixture drain. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (traps).

q: What is the minimum trap size for a floor drain?
n: Floor drain traps must be at least 50 mm (2 in.) in size. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (trap sizes); Uniform Plumbing Code Table 702.1.

q: Which of the following can discharge directly into the drainage system?
n: Fixture discharges flow through the building drain to the building sewer, which discharges directly into the public drainage system. Oil, grease and ashes are prohibited. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (prohibited wastes).

q: A drain carrying one or more fixtures to a soil or waste stack is a:
n: A branch drain is a horizontal drain carrying discharge from one or more fixtures to the soil or waste stack. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).

q: What is the allowable slope for a sanitary sewer?
n: Sanitary drains and sewers 75 mm and smaller are laid at 1/4 in. per foot (about 2%) for self-cleansing flow. Larger sizes may go to 1/8 in. per foot. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (slope of horizontal drainage).

q: Cleanouts are NOT required:
o: At a change in vertical direction
At a change in horizontal direction
n: Cleanouts are required at changes of horizontal direction greater than 45°, at intervals and at stack bases. They are not required where a line merely changes vertical direction. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (cleanouts).

q: What is the typical amount of waste discharged to a wastewater treatment facility?
n: Wastewater treatment facilities are rated by flow, and 300 gpm is a typical design discharge for a building's treatment system. Source: Metcalf & Eddy, Wastewater Engineering (design flows).

q: Under the Plumbing Code, horizontal drainage branches must slope at least:
n: Horizontal drainage branches must slope at least 2% (1/4 in. per foot). Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (slope of horizontal drainage).

q: What is the lowest horizontal pipe inside a building that collects fixture and branch discharge and carries it to the building sewer?
n: The building (house) drain is the lowest horizontal pipe inside the building, collecting all discharge. It runs to about 0.6 m outside the wall, where the building sewer begins. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).
